sources.work: Bigelow, Holtzman, Tanaka, Ullman. Forking Paths in Neural Text Generation. ICLR 2025 (arXiv 2412.07961)
sources.quote: a small set of 'forking tokens' exists, where resampling at those positions, but not elsewhere, produces very different outcomes (search summary of the ICLR text)
sources.verdict: METHOD SOURCE. Our locator is their prefix-resampling + Bayesian change-point recipe at lower density (S = 8 every 2 tokens). New here: the located token's tempered logits are used to PREDICT what temperature does to the algorithm before any temperature sample, and the prediction is scored.

sources.work: Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation (arXiv 2608.19611, 2026)
sources.quote: Regions around forking points show less accurate estimates when a wider stride is used.
sources.verdict: ADJACENT. Justifies our S = 8 / 2-token spacing as a cheaper-than-reference design and our single-token refinement around detected change points; we do not claim locator efficiency.

sources.work: Wang et al. Beyond the 80/20 Rule: High-Entropy Minority Tokens Drive Effective RL for LLM Reasoning. NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv 2506.01939)
sources.quote: these tokens semantically act as critical forks that steer the model toward diverse reasoning pathways
sources.verdict: RIVAL LOCATOR. Motivates the BH baseline (entropy-located decision position). Our decision tokens are located counterfactually and are often LOW-entropy (e.g. Gemma T04 'for' 0.73 / 'try' 0.10).

sources.work: Cantarero et al. The RLVR Policy Shift Is Sparse and Predictable from the Base Model. NeurIPS 2026 workshop
sources.quote: After RLVR, the disagreement between a trained model and its base is concentrated at only a small fraction of the positions they generate. We can identify these positions in advance using a single scalar: the base model's next-token entropy.
sources.verdict: ADJACENT, PARTLY OCCUPIED for the base sub-arm: 'post-training shifts concentrate at forks' is theirs (RLVR vs base, math). We claim only the counterfactually located decision token on code and the algorithm-level outcome, with their controls (entropy-matched, rate-matched random placement).

sources.quote: RL fine-tuning induces highly sparse and targeted changes, with only a small fraction of token distributions exhibiting meaningful divergence.
sources.verdict: ADJACENT (base-vs-post-trained token analysis); same caveat as Cantarero et al.

sources.work: Lin et al. The Unlocking Spell on Base LLMs (URIAL). ICLR 2024 (arXiv 2312.01552)
sources.quote: Base LLMs and their alignment-tuned versions perform nearly identically in decoding on the majority of token positions. Most distribution shifts occur with stylistic tokens.
sources.verdict: METHOD SOURCE for the base sub-arm (teacher forcing the base on the aligned model's outputs; rank categories 1 / 2-3 / >3).

sources.work: Lee, Chon, Jang, Lee, Yu. How Diversely Can Language Models Solve Problems? Exploring the Algorithmic Diversity of Model-Generated Code. Findings EMNLP 2025
sources.quote: model-generated solutions have low algorithmic diversity ... setting temperature above 1.0 can boost diversity
sources.verdict: CLOSEST BEHAVIOURAL WORK. They measure algorithm-level diversity vs temperature after the fact; we predict the per-temperature algorithm distribution in advance from one or two tokens and test the prediction on held-out units/families.

positioning_row: Temperature's effect on which algorithm an LLM writes is predicted IN ADVANCE, per unit and per temperature, by a frozen law over one or two counterfactually located decision tokens, and scored on held-out units in three model families against flat, algorithm-level-tempering, single-decision and entropy-located rivals. Adjacent and partly occupied: post-training shifts concentrating at forks (Cantarero et al.; Sparse but Critical); entropy forks (Beyond 80/20); forking-path resampling (Bigelow et al.; Forking Fast); algorithmic diversity vs temperature measured post hoc (Lee et al.).
